name: Civil unrest
value: France protests ebb; no deadly unrest
summary: French living-cost protests drew 82,500 on 21 Nov, the lowest yet; Indonesia detained 157 after 10 Nov clashes
state: France's interior ministry counted 82,500 protesters nationwide on 21 Nov, including 21,500 in Paris, the lowest turnout of six Saturdays of living-cost protests, with sporadic violence including in Marseille (Reuters via The Star). In Indonesia, police used rubber bullets and tear gas on anti-government protesters in Yogyakarta on 10 and 11 Nov and detained 157 people, most later released (Human Rights Watch). Significant protests in several countries keep Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest or major crackdown in a large country was found.
for_you: Travellers to France and Indonesia may meet road closures and transport disruption around protests. The FCDO publishes current travel advice for both countries.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests in several countries (France, Indonesia); no deadly nationwide unrest found

sources.title: The Star (Reuters) — Lower turnout at largely peaceful marches across France
Human Rights Watch — Indonesia: Alleged excessive force against protesters

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
